stem:
Meera is doing a science project at home in Jaipur. She wants to measure short intervals of time but does not have a stopwatch. She watches four processes happening around her and wonders which one could be used to measure time.

Which process can Meera use to measure time?

options.text: Raindrops falling from the roof at irregular intervals during a sudden shower.
A swing in the park moving back and forth, taking the same time for each complete to-and-fro movement.
A pressure cooker whistle that sounds once when the food is cooked.
Crackers bursting at random times during a Diwali celebration.

teacher.key_rationale: A process can measure time only if it repeats continuously after definite, equal intervals. The swing's regular to-and-fro motion provides a stable reference interval (like a pendulum), so counting its swings measures elapsed time — option B. The raindrops (A) and crackers (D) repeat but irregularly, so they cannot mark equal intervals; the cooker whistle (C) happens only once and does not repeat.
